ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-01.question: In Matthew 6:28, Jesus tells us to observe how the lilies of the field grow.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-01.learningObjective: Observe the image Jesus uses against anxiety about clothing.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-01.feedbackCorrect: Jesus points to the lilies: they neither toil nor spin, and still they grow.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Matthew 6:28: "Observem como os lírios do campo crescem".

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-01.hint: See the second sentence of the verse.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-02.question: In Matthew 6:24, tap the other master Jesus sets beside God.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-02.learningObjective: Identify riches as God's rival master.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-02.feedbackCorrect: Riches appear as a rival master: whoever serves them does not serve God wholly.

feedbackWrong.c: "Ninguém" (no one) opens the sentence; it is not God's rival.
feedbackWrong.a: "Desprezará" (will despise) is what happens to one master, not its name.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-02.hint: Look at the last sentence of the verse.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-03.question: According to Matthew 6:27, what can worry not add?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-03.learningObjective: Observe what Jesus says about the limit of worry.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-03.feedbackCorrect: Jesus asks who, by worrying, can lengthen their own life: no one.

feedbackWrong.b: Barns appear in 6:26, tied to the birds, not to worry.
feedbackWrong.a: Solomon appears in 6:29, compared with the lilies.
feedbackWrong.d: The verse speaks of the length of life, not of faith.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-03.hint: Read the end of Jesus' question.

options.c: A cubit to the length of life
options.b: More food to the barn
options.a: More beauty than Solomon's

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-04.question: Put Matthew 6:34 in the order of the text.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-04.feedbackCorrect: First the command, then the reason, and last the limit: each day with its own trouble.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the command not to worry; "basta a cada dia" closes the verse.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-04.hint: The verse begins with a command.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-05.question: In Matthew 6:26, where do the birds store nothing?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-05.learningObjective: Remember the detail that ties the birds to the theme of storing up.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-05.feedbackCorrect: The birds store no harvest, and still the Father feeds them.

feedbackWrong.c: Nests are not in the verse; the text speaks of where a harvest is kept.
feedbackWrong.a: Fields appear with the lilies, in 6:28.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-05.hint: Think of the place where a harvest is kept.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-06.question: What does Matthew 6:32 say that connects to this context?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-06.learningObjective: Connect Matthew 6:32 to the listeners' concrete worries.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-01-06.feedbackCorrect: Jesus doesn't say food and clothing don't matter: the Father knows we need them.

feedbackWrong.c: Jesus calls these things needs; he does not despise them.
feedbackWrong.a: The text says "vocês necessitam": the need is real.

options.b: The Father knows these needs
options.c: These needs do not matter
options.a: Believers have no needs

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-01.question: In Matthew 6:24–25, the command not to be anxious stands alone, unconnected to what Jesus said about riches.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-01.learningObjective: Understand the link between serving riches and living anxious.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-01.feedbackCorrect: "Por isso" (therefore) ties them: whoever serves riches ends up anxious about tomorrow.

feedbackWrong.true: Notice how 6:25 begins: "Por isso" links anxiety to what came before.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-01.hint: Look at the first two words of 6:25.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-02.question: In Matthew 6:30, tap the words that move the argument from lesser to greater.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-02.learningObjective: Recognize the argument from lesser to greater.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-02.feedbackCorrect: If God cares for grass that lasts a day, he will care far more for his children.

feedbackWrong.b: "Hoje existe" describes the passing grass; the argument turns later.
feedbackWrong.c: "Pequena fé" is Jesus' diagnosis, not the turning point of the argument.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-02.hint: Look for the comparison near the end of the verse.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-03.question: How does Matthew 6:24 prepare what Jesus says about anxiety in 6:25?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-03.learningObjective: Relate the lordship of riches to anxiety.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-03.feedbackCorrect: The master who rules the heart also dictates its worries; that is why Jesus links them.

feedbackWrong.a: Jesus speaks of serving riches as a master, not of condemning all money.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not say to work harder; it points to the Father who provides.
feedbackWrong.c: Body and clothing come in as examples of worry, not as a new subject.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-03.hint: Think about what it means to have riches as a master.

options.d: Whoever serves riches lives anxious about them
options.a: All money is sin and should be avoided
options.b: Working harder is the way not to fear
options.c: The subject shifts from the heart to the body

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-04.question: How do the steps of Matthew 6:31–33 connect?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-04.learningObjective: Understand how the argument moves from worry to seeking the kingdom.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-04.feedbackCorrect: Jesus swaps anxious questions for remembering the Father, and then for seeking the kingdom.

feedbackWrong.default: The reason comes in the middle (the Father knows); seeking the kingdom is the goal.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-04.hint: The "Pois" of 6:32 explains the command of 6:31.

options.a: Stop the anxious questions about food and clothing
options.b: Remember that the Father already knows each need
options.c: Put the kingdom of God first

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-05.question: In Matthew 6:33, what happens to the other things for those who seek the kingdom first?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-05.learningObjective: Understand the result of seeking the kingdom first.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-05.feedbackCorrect: They come along: the kingdom doesn't take away provision, it puts it in its place.

feedbackWrong.b: The text promises the opposite: nothing is taken from those who seek the kingdom.
feedbackWrong.a: There is no charge; the verb speaks of something given in addition.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-05.hint: The verb points to something given in addition.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-06.question: What links Matthew 6:26 to Psalms 147:9?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-06.learningObjective: Relate the Father's care in Matthew to the praise of the psalm.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-06.feedbackCorrect: Jesus echoes the psalm: God feeds even young ravens, and far more his children.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts stress food given by God, not the birds' effort.
feedbackWrong.c: Jesus says the opposite: you are worth much more than they.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-01-06.hint: Compare who feeds the birds in both texts.

options.b: God feeds even the young ravens
options.a: Birds work for their food
options.c: Animals are worth more than us

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-01.question: In Matthew 6:31–32, Jesus does not deny our needs; he places them under the care of the Father who knows them.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-01.learningObjective: Interpret that the Father's care, not the absence of need, answers anxiety.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-01.feedbackCorrect: The text calls food and clothing real needs and hands them to the Father who knows them.

feedbackWrong.false: Jesus says "vocês necessitam": the need is real; the answer is the Father, not denial.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-01.hint: See who knows the needs in 6:32.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-02.question: In Matthew 6:24, tap the phrase that shows riches competing for God's place.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-02.learningObjective: Show from the text that riches can become a master.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-02.feedbackCorrect: Riches are not just things: they can become a master that claims the heart.

feedbackWrong.a: "Ninguém" says it is impossible; who competes for God's place comes after.
feedbackWrong.c: "Aborrecer-se" shows the effect of the split, not who is competing.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-02.hint: Look for who is in dispute at the start of the verse.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-03.question: What reading of Matthew 6:34 holds up for someone anxious about tomorrow?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading of Matthew 6:34 the text supports.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-03.feedbackCorrect: Jesus admits each day has its trouble, but lifts tomorrow's weight off today.

feedbackWrong.c: Jesus speaks of anxiety that rules, not of careful planning.
feedbackWrong.d: The verse itself says each day brings its own trouble.
feedbackWrong.b: The context is the Father who knows and provides; no one is alone.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-03.hint: Notice what Jesus admits about each day.

options.a: Live today's day; tomorrow stays with the Father
options.c: Planning for the future is always a lack of faith
options.d: Whoever trusts God will have no trouble tomorrow
options.b: Each one carries the day's troubles alone

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-04.question: Which sequence reveals the logic of Matthew 6:21–25?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-04.learningObjective: See the logic linking treasure, lordship and anxiety.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-04.feedbackCorrect: Treasure, master and anxiety form a chain: what I keep decides what I fear.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the treasure (6:21); anxiety (6:25) is the end of the chain.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-04.hint: Follow the text: treasure, then masters, then anxiety.

options.a: What I keep as treasure pulls my heart
options.b: The heart that is pulled chooses whom to serve
options.c: Serving riches breeds anxiety about provision

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-05.question: In Matthew 6:33, what is sought together with the kingdom of God?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that goes with the kingdom in the disciple's search.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-05.feedbackCorrect: Kingdom and righteousness go together: seeking God is wanting what he deems right.

feedbackWrong.a: Riches are precisely the rival master of 6:24.
feedbackWrong.b: The text speaks of what God deems right, not of glory.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-05.hint: It is what God deems right.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-06.question: What links Matthew 6:32 to 1 Peter 5:7?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-06.learningObjective: Connect the Father's care in Matthew to the invitation of 1 Peter.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-06.feedbackCorrect: Peter echoes Jesus: worry goes to God, because he cares for you.

feedbackWrong.b: Both texts say the opposite: the Father knows and cares.
feedbackWrong.a: Peter does not forbid it; he invites us to cast our worry on God.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-01-06.hint: See the reason Peter gives for casting our worry.

options.c: Worry handed to the one who cares
options.b: God ignores our worries
options.a: Worrying is forbidden for Christians

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-01.question: In Philippians 4:6, Paul says to bring to God only the most important requests.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-01.learningObjective: Observe how far the invitation to prayer reaches.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-01.feedbackCorrect: Paul says "em tudo" (in everything): no worry is too small to bring to God.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread it: "em tudo" present your requests, not only in big things.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-01.hint: Notice how much goes into prayer.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-02.question: In Philippians 4:7, tap what God's peace will guard along with the heart.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-02.feedbackCorrect: God's peace guards the heart and also the thoughts.

feedbackWrong.b: Peace is the one guarding; what it guards comes after.
feedbackWrong.a: "Ultrapassa" (surpasses) describes the peace, not what it guards.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-02.hint: Look for what comes right after "coração".

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-03.question: According to Philippians 4:6, with what attitude should requests go to God?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-03.learningObjective: Observe the attitude that goes with prayer.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-03.feedbackCorrect: Paul asks for prayer and petition with thanksgiving: the request comes with gratitude.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of repeating; it speaks of giving thanks.
feedbackWrong.d: There is no bargain: requests go to God with gratitude.
feedbackWrong.b: Paul invites us to bring everything; there is no fear of bothering him.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-03.hint: Read the end of the verse.

options.c: With thanksgiving
options.a: With many repetitions
options.b: Afraid of being a bother

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-04.question: Put Philippians 4:6 in the order of the text.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-04.feedbackCorrect: First the "no" to anxiety, then prayer "in everything", and last the way to pray.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with anxiety; the way to pray, with thanksgiving, closes the verse.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-04.hint: The verse begins with a prohibition.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-05.question: In Philippians 4:12, what does Paul say he has also been, besides humbled?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-05.learningObjective: Remember the extremes Paul lived through.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-05.feedbackCorrect: Paul knew both sides: humiliation and honor.

feedbackWrong.a: Wealth appears as "abundância" further on; humbled is paired with something else.
feedbackWrong.b: The text speaks of standing before others, not of affection.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-05.hint: It is the opposite of humbled.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-06.question: What does Philippians 4:12 say that connects to this context?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-06.learningObjective: Connect Philippians 4:12 to Paul's real situation.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-06.feedbackCorrect: Paul is not speaking from afar: he has gone hungry and knows what it is to need help.

feedbackWrong.b: The verse says the opposite: he has experienced hunger and want.
feedbackWrong.c: He rejoices in the help (4:10); he just does not depend on it for peace.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-02-06.hint: See what experiences Paul says he has had.

options.a: Paul knows lack from the inside
options.b: Paul never went through need
options.c: Paul looks down on the help he got

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-01.question: In Philippians 4:6–7, God's peace appears as the result of bringing everything to God in prayer.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-01.learningObjective: Understand the relation between prayer and peace in Philippians 4:6–7.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-01.feedbackCorrect: The "E" (and) of 4:7 joins them: whoever brings everything to God receives the guarding peace.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread how 4:7 begins: the peace is tied to the prayer of 4:6.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-02.question: In Philippians 4:6, tap the word that turns the sentence from anxiety to prayer.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-02.learningObjective: Recognize the contrast marker in Philippians 4:6.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-02.feedbackCorrect: "Porém" (but) makes the turn: instead of anxiety about nothing, prayer in everything.

feedbackWrong.a: "Não estejam" is the prohibition; the turn comes after.
feedbackWrong.b: "Súplica" (petition) is part of prayer, not the word that makes the turn.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-02.hint: Look for the word between commas, in the middle of the verse.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-03.question: Why does Paul say in Philippians 4:11 that he is not speaking "out of need"?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-03.learningObjective: Relate Paul's gratitude to a contentment that does not depend on help.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-03.feedbackCorrect: Paul rejoices in the help, but his peace comes from having learned to be content.

feedbackWrong.b: In 4:12 he says he has gone through hunger and want.
feedbackWrong.d: He truly rejoices in the help (4:10).
feedbackWrong.c: The text does not mention stored goods; it speaks of learned contentment.

options.a: His peace does not depend on receiving help
options.b: He never went through any need
options.d: He did not want the Philippians' help
options.c: He had goods stored away in prison

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-04.question: How do the movements of Philippians 4:4–6 connect?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-04.learningObjective: Understand that the Lord's nearness prepares the invitation against anxiety.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-04.feedbackCorrect: The Lord's nearness comes before the request: because he is near, anxiety becomes prayer.

feedbackWrong.default: Prayer comes last; before it, joy and remembering that the Lord is near.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-04.hint: Anxiety appears after the Lord's nearness.

options.a: Rejoice in the Lord always
options.b: Remember that the Lord is near
options.c: Trade anxiety for prayer

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-05.question: In Philippians 4:7, what will God's peace do with the heart and the mind?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-05.learningObjective: Understand the effect of God's peace on those who pray.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-05.feedbackCorrect: Peace acts as a guard: it watches over the heart and mind of those who bring all to God.

feedbackWrong.b: Peace is a gift, not a charge.
feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of testing; it speaks of guarding.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-05.hint: Think of a sentry at the door.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-06.question: What links Philippians 4:7 to Isaiah 26:3?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-06.learningObjective: Relate the peace of Philippians to the promise of Isaiah.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, peace comes from God and keeps those who lean on him.

feedbackWrong.b: Neither text speaks of effort; peace comes from God.
feedbackWrong.a: Both place peace in God: "peace of God" and "trusts in you".

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-02-06.hint: Compare where the peace comes from and who receives it.

options.c: Peace kept for those who trust
options.b: Peace won by effort
options.a: Peace that leaves God out

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-01.question: In Philippians 4:11, Paul's contentment is a personality trait he was born with.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-01.learningObjective: Interpret contentment as something learned, not temperament.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-01.feedbackCorrect: Paul says "aprendi" (I learned): contentment is learned, in circumstances, with Christ.

feedbackWrong.true: The verb in 4:11 is "aprendi": it is not a trait from birth, it is learning.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-01.hint: Notice the verb before "a viver contente".

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-02.question: In Philippians 4:7, tap in whom the heart and mind are guarded.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-02.learningObjective: Show from the text that peace is tied to being in Christ.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-02.feedbackCorrect: The guarding happens in Christ: peace is not a technique, it is being united to him.

feedbackWrong.a: God's peace is the one guarding; where we are kept comes at the end.
feedbackWrong.c: The heart is what is being guarded, not where.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-02.hint: Look at the last words of the verse.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-03.question: For someone anxious about what is lacking, what reading of Philippians 4:12–13 holds up?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading of Philippians 4:13 the context supports.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-03.feedbackCorrect: "All things" includes the hunger and want of 4:12, lived with Christ's strength.

feedbackWrong.a: Read with 4:12, the verse is about going through plenty and hunger, not personal goals.
feedbackWrong.d: Paul says he knows hunger; Christ's strength does not erase it.
feedbackWrong.b: Paul rejoices in the church's help (4:10); contentment is not isolation.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-03.hint: Read 4:13 together with the situations of 4:12.

options.c: Christ sustains even when the lack goes on
options.a: With faith I will reach any goal I want
options.d: Whoever trusts never again feels hunger or need
options.b: Contentment means not needing anyone

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of Philippians 4:6–9?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-04.learningObjective: See how Paul leads from the peace of God to the God of peace.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-04.feedbackCorrect: From request to peace, and from peace to the God of peace himself: the gift leads to the giver.

feedbackWrong.default: Prayer comes first (4:6); the God of peace present (4:9) is the goal.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-04.hint: Follow 4:6 to 4:9: the request, the gift, the giver.

options.a: Bring everything to God in grateful prayer
options.b: Receive the peace that comes from God
options.c: Have the God of peace himself near

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-05.question: In Philippians 4:7, what does God's peace surpass?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-05.learningObjective: Remember the term showing that God's peace goes beyond understanding.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-05.feedbackCorrect: God's peace goes beyond what the mind can explain: it arrives before the answers.

feedbackWrong.c: The text speaks of something the mind tries to reach, not a feeling.
feedbackWrong.a: It is not distance: it is the limit of what we can understand.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-05.hint: Think of what the mind tries to reach when explaining.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-06.question: What links Philippians 4:13 to John 15:5?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-06.learningObjective: Connect the strength of Philippians 4:13 to union with Christ in John 15.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-06.feedbackCorrect: Paul can do it through Christ; Jesus says without him we can do nothing: strength comes from him.

feedbackWrong.b: Both texts place the source outside us: "him" and "in me".
feedbackWrong.a: Jesus says the opposite: apart from him we can do nothing.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-02-06.hint: Compare where the ability comes from in both texts.

options.c: Strength that comes from Christ
options.b: Strength that comes from within
options.a: Fruit without depending on anyone

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-01.question: In Psalms 23:2, the psalmist is the one who looks for the green pastures on his own.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-01.learningObjective: Observe that rest is the shepherd's work.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-01.feedbackCorrect: The shepherd is the one acting: "Ele me faz repousar" and "leva-me" to the waters.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread 23:2: he, the shepherd, makes him lie down and leads him to the waters.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-01.hint: Notice who is the subject of the verbs.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-02.question: In Psalms 23:2, tap what the shepherd makes the psalmist do in the pastures.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-02.learningObjective: Identify rest as the shepherd's care.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-02.feedbackCorrect: In the pastures, the shepherd makes the sheep rest: rest is given.

feedbackWrong.b: "Leva-me" (leads me) is the shepherd guiding to the waters, not what the sheep does.
feedbackWrong.a: "Águas" (waters) is where he leads, not the action in the pastures.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-02.hint: Look for the verb right after "Ele me faz".

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-03.question: According to Psalms 23:4, what comforts the psalmist in the valley?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-03.learningObjective: Observe what brings comfort to the psalmist in the valley.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-03.feedbackCorrect: The tools of the shepherd, who guides and protects, are the comfort in the valley.

feedbackWrong.d: The text does not say the shadow disappears; it says the shepherd is there.
feedbackWrong.a: Friends do not appear; the one with him is the shepherd.
feedbackWrong.b: There is no quick exit in the verse; he walks through the valley.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-03.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

options.c: The shepherd's rod and staff
options.d: The light that drives away the shadow
options.a: The company of friends
options.b: A quick way out of danger

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-04.question: Put Psalms 23:5 in the order of the text.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-04.feedbackCorrect: Banquet, oil and a full cup: care shows up with enemies still nearby.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the banquet; the overflowing cup closes the verse.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-04.hint: The verse begins with a table being prepared.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-05.question: In Psalms 23:1, what does the psalmist say of himself, with the Lord as shepherd?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-05.learningObjective: Remember the trust that opens the psalm.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-05.feedbackCorrect: With the Lord as shepherd, he does not lack the care he needs.

feedbackWrong.b: The text speaks of lack, not of surplus.
feedbackWrong.a: Nothing is charged to the sheep; the care comes from the shepherd.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-05.hint: Think of what a well-tended sheep does not feel.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-06.question: What does Psalms 23:1–2 say that connects to this context?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-06.learningObjective: Connect the image of the shepherd in Psalms 23:1–2 to what David knew.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-06.feedbackCorrect: David knew what shepherding is: calling the Lord shepherd speaks of close care.

feedbackWrong.c: A shepherd walks with the flock; he does not watch from afar.
feedbackWrong.a: In the psalm, all the verbs of care belong to the shepherd.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-03-06.hint: Think of what a shepherd does with the sheep.

options.b: God guides and protects up close
options.c: God watches from afar
options.a: The sheep fends for itself

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-01.question: In Psalms 23:1–2, rest in the pastures shows in practice what "nada me faltará" means.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-01.feedbackCorrect: Verse 2 explains verse 1: what is not lacking is rest, pasture and water from the shepherd.

feedbackWrong.false: Read 23:1 and 23:2 together: the rest and the waters show what is not lacking.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-01.hint: Read verse 2 as an explanation of verse 1.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-02.question: In Psalms 23:4, tap the words that admit the valley will come.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-02.learningObjective: Recognize the concession marker in Psalms 23:4.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-02.feedbackCorrect: Trust does not deny danger: the psalmist admits the valley and lives with it.

feedbackWrong.c: "Não temerei" (I will fear no) is the response to the valley, not the admission of it.
feedbackWrong.a: "Me confortam" (comfort me) speaks of comfort, which comes later.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-02.hint: Look at the beginning of the verse.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-03.question: How does the valley of Psalms 23:4 connect to the paths of righteousness in 23:3?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-03.learningObjective: Relate the shepherd's leading to the passage through the valley.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-03.feedbackCorrect: The shepherd leads on right paths, and the valley lies on the way; he does not abandon us there.

feedbackWrong.c: The text does not tie the valley to punishment; the psalmist walks it led.
feedbackWrong.d: The shepherd is in the valley: "tu estás comigo".
feedbackWrong.b: The psalmist walks through the valley while being led on the right paths.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-03.hint: See who leads in 23:3 and who is with him in 23:4.

options.a: The shepherd's right path also goes through the valley
options.c: The valley is punishment for leaving the paths
options.d: The valley lies far from the shepherd's path
options.b: The right paths avoid every dark valley

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-04.question: In what order does the shepherd care for the sheep in Psalms 23:1–3?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement of care in Psalms 23:1–3.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-04.feedbackCorrect: First who cares, then rest, then direction: from rest to the road.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with who cares (23:1); direction on the right path comes last.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-04.hint: The psalm begins by saying who the shepherd is.

options.a: The psalmist declares who cares for him
options.b: The shepherd gives rest and water
options.c: The shepherd leads on the right path

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-05.question: In Psalms 23:3, what does the shepherd do with the psalmist's soul?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-05.learningObjective: Understand the shepherd's action on the soul.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-05.feedbackCorrect: The shepherd refreshes the weary soul, like cool water after the road.

feedbackWrong.b: The text speaks of relief, not of examination.
feedbackWrong.a: The shepherd does the opposite: he renews the soul.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-05.hint: It is a verb of relief, like cool water.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-06.question: What links Psalms 23:1 to Philippians 4:19?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-06.learningObjective: Relate the trust of the psalm to the promise in Philippians.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-06.feedbackCorrect: Both texts place provision in God: what is lacking, he supplies.

feedbackWrong.c: Paul speaks of needs, not of every desire.
feedbackWrong.a: The riches are God's ("his riches in glory"); he supplies, he does not demand.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-03-06.hint: Compare what is not lacking and what God supplies.

options.b: God supplies our needs
options.c: God fulfills every desire
options.a: God expects our wealth

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-01.question: In Psalms 23:1, "nada me faltará" is trust in the shepherd, not a formula to recite against problems.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-01.learningObjective: Interpret Psalm 23 as trust, not as a charm.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-01.feedbackCorrect: Security lies in the one who shepherds, not in the words; the psalm is relationship, not a charm.

feedbackWrong.false: The psalm places trust in the shepherd; repeating words does not replace trusting him.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-01.hint: Notice who the verse places at the center.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-02.question: In Psalms 23:6, tap the phrase that shows God's goodness going after the psalmist.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-02.learningObjective: Show from the text that God's care accompanies the psalmist.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-02.feedbackCorrect: God's goodness goes after the psalmist, like someone who never loses sight of him.

feedbackWrong.a: "Todos os dias" (all the days) says how long, not the movement of following.
feedbackWrong.b: "Casa do Senhor" (house of the Lord) is the destination, not goodness moving.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-02.hint: Look for the verb of movement.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-03.question: What reading of Psalms 23:2 holds up about rest?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading about rest that the text supports.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-03.feedbackCorrect: The shepherd makes him lie down and leads: rest is care received, not a prize earned.

feedbackWrong.a: The shepherd himself leads to rest; resting is part of his care.
feedbackWrong.c: The psalm puts rest before the valley and the enemies, not after.
feedbackWrong.b: Sheep need rest; the psalm assumes weariness and cares for it.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-03.hint: See who makes the rest happen.

options.d: Rest is given by the shepherd, who leads to it
options.a: Resting is a lack of faith in one who should fight
options.c: Rest only comes when the problems end
options.b: Whoever has faith never feels tired

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-04.question: Which sequence reveals how Psalm 23 deals with fear?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-04.learningObjective: See the path from fear to trust in Psalm 23.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-04.feedbackCorrect: The psalm starts in trust, passes through the valley and ends in goodness that follows.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the psalm: trust (23:1), valley (23:4), goodness to the end (23:6).

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-04.hint: Follow the psalm from beginning to end.

options.a: Trust the one who cares before the danger
options.b: Walk through the valley without denying the shadow
options.c: Expect the goodness that follows to the end

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-05.question: In Psalms 23:4, where does the psalmist admit he walks?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-05.learningObjective: Remember the term showing where the shepherd goes with us.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-05.feedbackCorrect: The dark place is real in the psalm: the shepherd doesn't take the sheep out, he walks with it.

feedbackWrong.b: The text speaks of a low, dark place, not a high one.
feedbackWrong.a: The place is marked by the shadow of death, between slopes.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-05.hint: Think of a low, narrow, dark place.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-06.question: What links Psalms 23:3 to Matthew 11:29?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-06.learningObjective: Connect the shepherd of the psalm to the rest Jesus offers.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-06.feedbackCorrect: The shepherd refreshes the soul; Jesus promises rest for the soul of whoever comes to him.

feedbackWrong.b: Neither text speaks of effort; both speak of relief given.
feedbackWrong.a: Jesus says he is gentle and humble; he calls the weary.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-03-06.hint: Compare what both texts promise to the soul.

options.c: Rest for the soul
options.b: A soul saved by effort
options.a: A heavy yoke for the strong

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-01.question: In Matthew 6:7, Jesus says not to use vain repetitions when praying.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-01.learningObjective: Observe what Jesus says to avoid in prayer.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-01.feedbackCorrect: Jesus cuts off the idea that many words guarantee being heard.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-01.hint: See the beginning of the verse.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-02.question: In Matthew 6:9, tap where the Father to whom the prayer is addressed is.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-02.learningObjective: Identify to whom and where the prayer is directed.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-02.feedbackCorrect: The Father is "ours", near, and above all at the same time.

feedbackWrong.a: "Teu nome" (your name) is what is asked to be hallowed, not where the Father is.
feedbackWrong.c: "Desta forma" (in this way) introduces the prayer; it does not say where the Father is.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-02.hint: Look for a place right after "que estás".

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-03.question: According to Matthew 6:7, what did the Gentiles assume when praying?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-03.learningObjective: Observe the mistake Jesus corrects in prayer.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-03.feedbackCorrect: They thought the number of words guaranteed an answer.

feedbackWrong.c: That is what Jesus says of the Father in 6:8, not what the Gentiles thought.
feedbackWrong.a: Praying in secret is Jesus' teaching (6:6), not the Gentiles' idea.
feedbackWrong.b: The verse does not speak of forgiveness; it speaks of many words.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-03.hint: Read the end of the verse.

options.d: That they would be heard for speaking much
options.c: That God already knew everything
options.a: That they should pray in secret
options.b: That forgiveness came before bread

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-04.question: Put Matthew 6:8 in the order of the text.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-04.feedbackCorrect: The command, the reason and the detail: the Father knows even before we ask.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with "Não vos assemelheis a eles"; "antes mesmo" closes the verse.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-04.hint: The verse begins with a prohibition.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-05.question: In Matthew 6:11, for when is the bread asked?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-05.learningObjective: Remember for when Jesus teaches us to ask for bread.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-05.feedbackCorrect: Jesus teaches us to ask for this day's bread, not the month's stockpile.

feedbackWrong.c: "Sempre" (always) would ask for everything at once; the text asks for the day's bread.
feedbackWrong.a: The text does not ask for haste; it asks for this day's bread.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-05.hint: Think of the shortest time possible.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-06.question: What does Matthew 6:11 say that connects to this context?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-06.learningObjective: Connect Matthew 6:11 to the life of those who lived on a daily wage.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-06.feedbackCorrect: For those living on a daily wage, asking for daily bread was handing today to the Father.

feedbackWrong.c: The request is for the day's bread, not for a stockpile.
feedbackWrong.b: The text says "Dá-nos" (give us): the request includes the one praying.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-06.hint: Notice the measure of time in the request.

options.a: Depending on God each day
options.c: Securing a stockpile for the month
options.b: Praying only for other people's needs

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-01.question: In Matthew 6:8, Jesus says we must pray a lot so the Father finds out what we need.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-01.learningObjective: Understand the relation between the Father's knowing and prayer.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-01.feedbackCorrect: It is the opposite: we pray because the Father already knows, not to inform him.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread 6:8: the Father knows "antes mesmo de lho pedirdes" (before you ask).

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-02.question: In Matthew 6:8, tap the word that introduces the reason not to pray like the Gentiles.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-02.learningObjective: Recognize the cause marker in Matthew 6:8.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-02.feedbackCorrect: It brings the reason: do not imitate the Gentiles, because the Father already knows.

feedbackWrong.a: "Antes" (before) says when the Father knows; the reason starts earlier.
feedbackWrong.b: "Não" (do not) opens the prohibition; the reason comes after.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-02.hint: Look right after the first comma.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-03.question: In Matthew 6:10–11, what does the order of the requests teach about bread?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-03.learningObjective: Relate the order of the requests to the place of bread.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-03.feedbackCorrect: Kingdom and will come first; bread comes after, within that care.

feedbackWrong.b: Jesus tells us to ask for bread: it matters to the Father.
feedbackWrong.c: In the text, bread comes after the name, the kingdom and the will.
feedbackWrong.d: The text does not tie the coming of the kingdom to surplus bread.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-03.hint: See the order: kingdom and will, then bread.

options.a: Bread is asked within the kingdom, not in its place
options.b: Bread matters little to God
options.c: Bread should be asked for before everything
options.d: The kingdom only comes when there is bread to spare

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-04.question: In what order does the prayer go from the Father to the bread in Matthew 6:9–11?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement of the prayer from the Father to the bread.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-04.feedbackCorrect: First who God is, then his kingdom, and only then today's bread.

feedbackWrong.default: Bread comes last; the prayer begins with who God is.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-04.hint: The prayer begins with the name of the one who hears.

options.a: Call God Father in heaven
options.b: Ask for God's kingdom to come to earth
options.c: Ask for bread just for this day

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-05.question: In Matthew 6:9, which word links the teaching of 6:8 to the prayer that follows?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-05.learningObjective: Understand prayer as a consequence of the Father's care.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-05.feedbackCorrect: Prayer is a consequence: the Father knows, so pray like this, with trust.

feedbackWrong.c: "Contudo" (however) would set up a contrast; prayer follows from 6:8.
feedbackWrong.b: "Todavia" (yet) signals contrast; the text draws a conclusion.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-05.hint: It is a word of conclusion.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-06.question: What links Matthew 6:11 to Exodus 16:4?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-06.learningObjective: Relate daily bread to the manna in the desert.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-06.feedbackCorrect: In the desert, manna came as each day's portion; Jesus teaches us to ask the same way.

feedbackWrong.b: Manna was not for stockpiling; each day's portion came.
feedbackWrong.a: In both texts, bread is given by God, not earned.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-06.hint: Compare how often the bread arrives.

options.c: Provision given day by day
options.b: Bread stored up for the year
options.a: Bread earned by merit

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-01.question: In Matthew 6:11, asking for bread "hoje" (today) means it is wrong to plan or save for the future.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-01.learningObjective: Interpret today's bread as dependence, not a ban on planning.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-01.feedbackCorrect: The request teaches daily dependence, not a ban on planning; what goes is the stockpile of fear.

feedbackWrong.true: Jesus teaches trust in the Father today; the text does not condemn prudent planning.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-01.hint: Think of what the request teaches, not what it forbids.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-02.question: In Matthew 6:11, tap the phrase showing that provision is asked again every morning.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-02.learningObjective: Show from the text that dependence is daily.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-02.feedbackCorrect: Provision is renewed at the pace of the day, like the manna in the desert.

feedbackWrong.c: "Nosso pão" (our bread) says what is asked, not the rhythm of asking.
feedbackWrong.b: "Dá-nos" (give us) shows it is a gift, but not the daily rhythm.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-02.hint: Look for the time expression at the end of the verse.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-03.question: What reading of Matthew 6:8 holds up for someone who prays anxiously?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading of Matthew 6:8 the context supports.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-03.feedbackCorrect: Whoever prays need not convince: the Father already knows the need before we ask.

feedbackWrong.b: Jesus concludes the opposite: "therefore", pray like this (6:9).
feedbackWrong.d: Jesus rejects the idea of being heard for many words (6:7).
feedbackWrong.c: The text rests security on the Father who knows, not on the wording.

options.a: I can pray with few words, for the Father knows
options.b: If the Father already knows, I need not pray
options.d: The more I repeat, the more I will be heard
options.c: God only hears well-worded requests

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-04.question: Which sequence reveals the thread of daily bread in the Bible?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-04.learningObjective: See Matthew 6:11 within the thread of bread in the Bible.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-04.feedbackCorrect: Daily manna prepares the request for bread, and both point to Jesus, the bread of life.

feedbackWrong.default: Start in the desert (Ex 16); the bread of life (Jn 6:35) is the goal.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-04.hint: Follow the Bible story: desert, Sermon on the Mount, John 6.

options.a: God sends manna day after day in the desert
options.b: Jesus teaches us to ask for today's bread
options.c: Jesus presents himself as the bread of life

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-05.question: In Matthew 6:10, what is asked to be done on earth as in heaven?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries surrender to God in prayer.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-05.feedbackCorrect: Asking God to rule also over what we cannot control takes command away from fear.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of a word; it speaks of what God wants.
feedbackWrong.c: What is asked to be done is what God wants, not a work.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-06.question: What links Matthew 6:8 to Isaiah 65:24?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-06.learningObjective: Connect the Father who knows in Matthew to the promise of Isaiah.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-06.feedbackCorrect: Isaiah and Jesus say the same: God knows and answers before we finish asking.

feedbackWrong.c: Both texts say the opposite: God answers beforehand.
feedbackWrong.a: Jesus rejects many words; Isaiah says God hears while they are still speaking.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-06.hint: Compare when God hears in both texts.

options.b: God hears before the request
options.c: God is slow to answer
options.a: God hears whoever talks most

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-01.question: In 1 Peter 1:6, Peter says the readers are grieved by various trials.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-01.learningObjective: Observe that Peter acknowledges the readers' grief.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-01.feedbackCorrect: Peter does not hide the pain: the readers are sad because of various trials.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the end of 1 Peter 1:6: "entristecidos por diversas provações".

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-01.hint: See the end of the verse.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-02.question: In 1 Peter 1:3, tap the measure by which God gave us new birth.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-02.learningObjective: Identify God's mercy as the origin of the new birth.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-02.feedbackCorrect: The new birth comes from the greatness of God's love: it is a gift, not merit.

feedbackWrong.a: "Nosso Senhor" (our Lord) names Jesus; the measure of the new birth is something else.
feedbackWrong.b: "Dentre os mortos" (from the dead) speaks of Jesus' resurrection, not God's measure.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-02.hint: Look for what comes after "segundo a sua".

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-03.question: According to 1 Peter 1:7, what does Peter compare tested faith to?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-03.learningObjective: Observe the image Peter uses for tested faith.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-03.feedbackCorrect: Tested faith is like gold in the fire, and even more precious than it.

feedbackWrong.c: The text speaks of neither silver nor temple.
feedbackWrong.d: The image of seed is not here; Peter uses a metal in the fire.
feedbackWrong.b: The house on the rock is Jesus' image in Matthew 7, not this verse.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-03.hint: Think of a metal that goes through fire.

options.a: To gold tested by fire
options.c: To silver kept in the temple
options.d: To seed sown in the ground
options.b: To a house set on the rock

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-04.question: Put 1 Peter 1:8 in the order of the text.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-04.feedbackCorrect: Loving without seeing, believing without seeing, and then joy: that is the verse's sequence.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with "A quem, não o tendo visto, amais"; joy closes the verse.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-04.hint: The verse begins by speaking of love.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-05.question: In 1 Peter 1:4, how is the inheritance kept in heaven?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-05.learningObjective: Remember where and how the inheritance is kept.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-05.feedbackCorrect: The inheritance has a guaranteed owner and place, far from what spoils.

feedbackWrong.c: It is not hidden; it is set apart for you.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of postponement; it speaks of something kept.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-05.hint: Think of a table set aside with your name on it.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-06.question: What does 1 Peter 1:6 say that connects to this context?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-06.learningObjective: Connect 1 Peter 1:6 to the readers' situation.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-06.feedbackCorrect: Peter names the grief and the trials: hope does not begin by denying pain.

feedbackWrong.a: The text says they are grieved, and Peter does not rebuke them for it.
feedbackWrong.b: Peter says "no presente" (now): the trials are happening.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-05-06.hint: See how Peter describes what they feel.

options.c: Peter takes their pain seriously
options.a: Christians should not be sad
options.b: The trials were already over

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-01.question: In 1 Peter 1:5, salvation has already been fully revealed, and there is nothing left to hope for.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-01.learningObjective: Understand that God's keeping points to a future.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-01.feedbackCorrect: Salvation is "prestes a se revelar" (ready to be revealed): there is a future kept by God.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the end of 1:5: salvation is yet to be revealed in the last time.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-01.hint: See the end of the verse.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-02.question: In 1 Peter 1:6, tap the word that holds joy and grief together at the same time.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-02.learningObjective: Recognize the contrast marker in 1 Peter 1:6.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-02.feedbackCorrect: The word holds both together: they rejoice and they are sad.

feedbackWrong.c: "Nisso" (in this) points to the reason for joy, not to the contrast.
feedbackWrong.b: "Breve tempo" (a little while) says how long grief lasts, not what links the two.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-02.hint: Look for the word between commas after "exultam".

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-03.question: How does 1 Peter 1:5 complete what 1:4 says about the inheritance?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-03.learningObjective: Relate the kept inheritance to the kept heirs.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-03.feedbackCorrect: The inheritance is reserved in heaven, and those who believe are kept until they get there.

feedbackWrong.a: 1:5 says those who believe are also being guarded.
feedbackWrong.b: Faith is the means; the one who guards is God.
feedbackWrong.d: Salvation is revealed "in the last time", not all now.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-03.hint: See who is being guarded in 1:5.

options.c: The inheritance is kept, and so are the heirs
options.a: Only the inheritance is safe; the rest is up to us
options.b: The believer's faith is what holds everything
options.d: The inheritance will be handed over in full in this life

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-04.question: How do the movements of 1 Peter 1:5–7 connect?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement from God's keeping to tested faith.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-04.feedbackCorrect: Kept by God, tested for a while, and faith ends in praise.

feedbackWrong.default: God's keeping comes first (1:5); praise (1:7) is the goal.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-04.hint: Start with what God does in 1:5.

options.a: God guards those who believe to the end
options.b: Those who believe go through trials
options.c: Tested faith ends in praise

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-05.question: In 1 Peter 1:7, what happens to gold, in contrast with faith?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-05.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between gold and tested faith.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-05.feedbackCorrect: Gold runs out; tested faith is worth more because it remains.

feedbackWrong.a: Shining would be praise; the text shows gold's limit.
feedbackWrong.b: Gold does not grow; the contrast is with something that ends.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-05.hint: It is the opposite of lasting.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-06.question: What links 1 Peter 1:6 to 2 Corinthians 4:17?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-06.learningObjective: Relate the brief grief of 1 Peter to the glory of 2 Corinthians.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-06.feedbackCorrect: Peter and Paul weigh pain against the future: brief next to the coming glory.

feedbackWrong.b: Both texts give affliction meaning: it is not the last word.
feedbackWrong.a: Both admit affliction; glory comes after it.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-05-06.hint: Compare how long the grief lasts in both texts.

options.c: Brief affliction, eternal glory
options.b: Affliction with no meaning at all
options.a: Glory without going through affliction

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-01.question: 1 Peter 1:6–7 lets us see trial as something God uses, not as a sign he has abandoned the one who suffers.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-01.feedbackCorrect: The "para que" (so that) gives trial a purpose: it is not abandonment, it happens under God's keeping.

feedbackWrong.false: Peter gives trial a purpose ("para que"); the text does not treat it as abandonment.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-02.question: In 1 Peter 1:5, tap the phrase that shows whose strength guards those who believe.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-02.learningObjective: Show from the text that God is the one who guards believers.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-02.feedbackCorrect: Security does not depend on the believer's strength: the one who guards is God.

feedbackWrong.b: Faith is the means by which the keeping is received; the strength comes from another.
feedbackWrong.c: "Último tempo" (last time) says when salvation is revealed, not who guards.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-02.hint: Look for who guards, not the means.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-03.question: What reading of 1 Peter 1:6 holds up about grief and hope?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading of 1 Peter 1:6 the text supports.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-03.feedbackCorrect: Peter joins joy and grief in the same verse, without rebuking those who weep.

feedbackWrong.d: The text says they rejoice though grieved; the two live together.
feedbackWrong.b: Peter does not call grief weak faith; he calls faith precious (1:7).
feedbackWrong.c: Those who suffer are being guarded by God (1:5).

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-03.hint: See the two things the verse holds together.

options.a: Hope can rejoice even through tears
options.d: Whoever has hope should not be sad
options.b: Sadness proves that faith is weak
options.c: Trial shows that God has drawn away

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-04.question: Which sequence reveals the path of faith in 1 Peter 1:3–9?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-04.learningObjective: See the path of faith from beginning to end in 1 Peter 1.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-04.feedbackCorrect: From new birth to final salvation, through testing: faith has a beginning, a way and an end.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with mercy (1:3); the salvation of souls (1:9) is the end of the path.

options.a: God's mercy gives a new beginning
options.b: Faith is tested in the midst of grief
options.c: Faith reaches its goal, salvation

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-05.question: In 1 Peter 1:3, what kind of hope does God give us in giving us new birth?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries the meaning of Christian hope.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-05.feedbackCorrect: Hope does not die because it rests on Jesus, who rose from the dead.

feedbackWrong.a: It is not vague: it is grounded in Jesus' resurrection.
feedbackWrong.b: It is not fragile: it springs from the power that raised Jesus.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-05.hint: Think of what the resurrection brings back.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-06.question: What links 1 Peter 1:5 to John 10:28?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-06.learningObjective: Connect the keeping in 1 Peter to Jesus' promise in John 10.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-06.feedbackCorrect: Peter says God guards; Jesus says no one snatches his sheep out of his hand.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts place the keeping in God, not in us.
feedbackWrong.c: Jesus speaks of all his sheep, not only the strong.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-05-06.hint: Compare who holds on and who tries to take away.

options.b: No one snatches those God keeps
options.a: Salvation depends only on us
options.c: God keeps only the strongest
